newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FOCUS - Output, order data show flat Taiwan recovery.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Output, order data show flat Taiwan recovery.

text.p: Strength in the star electronics industry ensured stable growth in Taiwan's April export orders and industrial output, but economists cautioned on Wednesday that a hard-won broader recovery had hit a plateau.

"The strong performance by the electronics industry had well covered the negative impact of the hog foot-and-mouth disease, but the overall economic recovery should remain flat in the first half," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.
Economists said the hog epidemic and growing perceptions of a decline in Taiwan's social order were key factors checking what two months ago had looked to be an accelerating recovery.
In its monthly report on Wednesday, the economics ministry said foreign orders for Taiwan goods hit US$10.490 billion in April, a 5.91 percent rise compared to April 1996.
While modest in percentage terms, the export orders rise surpassed an average forecast for a 2.548 percent rise that resulted from a May 20 Reuters poll of Taiwan economists.

The total value was the second highest ever, only slightly less than a record US$10.51 billion in September 1996 and reflecting growing demand for telecommunication and information products, orders for which rose 30.3 percent year-on-year.

Orders from Japan, which had been Taiwan's main market for pork exports, fell an annual 14.38 percent to $1.19 billion, due mainly to a flat ban on pork exports from March 20, when the hog foot and mouth epidemic was first detected.
The ministry said Taiwan's industrial output in April rose 6.12 percent compared to April 1996.
The rise in April industrial output was only slightly lower than an average forecast for a 6.902 percent year-on-year rise compiled from the May 20 Reuters poll.
Among industrial sectors, information and electronics had the highest growth, rising 11.61 percent from a year earlier.

Economists said the strong electronics orders -- which become actual exports in two to three months -- accorded with forecasts that the industry would have flat performance in the second quarter, with strong growth starting from June.
They cautioned that too much focus on a specific industry's growth was no guarantee of a wider recovery.
"It's good the electronics industry continues its strong performance, but other industries have not caught up with the recovery train," said HSBC James Capel economist Stephen Wang.
"So, we haven't seen a strong overall recovery yet."

Economists noted growing signs of a bottoming-out in the beleaguered property market, as April's index of construction firms that have sought development permits rose 43.02 percent year-on-year, the fifth straight monthly rise.
Real estate and construction output rose an annual 3.95 percent in April, reversing the incessant negative growth seen in recent years.
"Surely the property market is bottoming out," said Nomura's Huang. "Whether it's really recovering remains to be watched."

Huang said potential homebuyers, recently nosing around the market, had again become cautious due to a political firestorm over a spate of unsolved murders and a general belief that social order in Taiwan was slipping.
